_meta.unit: BODY LENGTH = 1.0 (point of chest / base of neck to point of buttock / ischium, side view, adult, neutral standing or resting pose). For shark: snout tip to caudal fin base. For frog: snout-vent length. For tortoise: straight carapace length. For crocodile: back of skull to vent (trunk only).
_meta.heights: vertical from ground; lengths are straight bone/segment lengths unless noted. Ranges are [lo, hi] across typical adults of the reference species.

reference_species.horse: light riding horse (Thoroughbred / warmblood), not draft or pony
reference_species.elephant: African bush elephant; Asian notes inline
reference_species.crocodile: Nile / saltwater crocodile, resting with belly down
reference_species.tortoise: sulcata / Galapagos-type land tortoise, head out, standing
reference_species.kangaroo: red kangaroo, resting upright on hind feet + tail tripod

_meta.source: written from memory by an anatomy-for-game-art pass; values are canonical artist proportions, not measured specimens

must_have: Leg length (ground to elbow) >= chest depth: elbow sits at or above the vertical midpoint of withers height. Wolves are leggy; a husky-like 50/50 split reads as a dog.
Tail hangs straight or slightly curved, tip reaching the hock; carried below the backline in neutral. Never curled over the back.
Narrow, deep chest viewed from the front (front legs close together, elbows tucked), big front paws (~0.08 wide), slightly sloping croup.
mistakes: Too stocky and broad-chested (sled-dog / German-shepherd build) with short legs.
Tail curled or carried high; tail too thin at the base.
Head too round with a short muzzle and oversized pointed ears; wolf muzzle is ~half the head length and ears are small (~1/3 head length) and rounded.

must_have: Square canon: withers height ~= body length ~= 2.5 head lengths; chest depth = half the height, elbow at that midpoint.
Knee (carpus) and hock at matching heights (~0.3); cannon bones are short and straight, ~half the forearm/gaskin.
Head length ~= chest depth; eye sits ~1/3 down from the poll; ear ~1/3 head length.
mistakes: Legs too short / barrel too deep (pony or cartoon proportions) and cannons too long relative to forearm.
Neck too short, too thick at the throat, or set too low; neck should be ~1 head long and tie in high at the withers.
Hooves too small and pasterns vertical; hoof width ~0.12 and pastern slopes ~45-50 degrees matching the shoulder.

must_have: African: highest point at the shoulder with a concave 'saddle' back; ear top reaches above the eye and ear bottom reaches the jaw/neck line; ear area ~0.15 body-length squared. Asian: domed twin-lobed forehead, convex back highest at the middle, ears ~half the size.
Trunk reaches the ground (~0.65-0.7) with the tip just clearing it in neutral stance; trunk base is as wide as the face.

Forelimb joints: elbow bends backward, wrist (the visible front 'knee') bends forward like a human wrist, hind limb has a true knee (stifle) high under the body and the hock low. Front feet round, hind feet oval, both nearly flush-sided cylinders.
mistakes: Legs too short and stubby with 'knees' bending the wrong way or both pairs bending the same way.
Ears too small (or African ears on an Asian body shape and vice versa); forgetting ears attach along the whole side of the head, not just at a point.
Trunk too short or too thin at the base; tusks sprouting from the mouth instead of from the upper jaw above and ahead of the mouth.

must_have: Neck ~= body length and the shoulder/withers hump is a tall spine-process ridge well forward; the back slopes steeply down to the croup (hip ~85-90% of withers).
Front legs only slightly longer than hind (the slope comes from the withers ridge, not from drastically different leg lengths); cannons are as long as the forearm/gaskin.
Ossicones 0.06-0.1 body length with knobbed tips, a median bump on the forehead; big dark eyes with long lashes set high and wide.
mistakes: Neck emerging from the middle of the back or too low on the chest; it should rise from the withers ridge with the chest sloping into it.
Hind legs drawn far shorter than front; hock placed too low (hock sits ~0.55, i.e. around belly height).
Horse-like head and horse-like leg joints; giraffe legs are thin and straight with very long cannons and the knee/hock far above the midpoint.

must_have: Tail ~45-50% of total length, oval-tall at the base (taller than wide), with two rows of raised scutes that merge into a single keel ~40% down the tail.
Hind limbs much larger than fore (thigh+shin ~0.4 vs arm ~0.3), sprawled outward at rest; 5 fingers front (3 clawed), 4 toes hind (webbed).
Flat skull table with eyes, ears and nostrils on one plane; 4th lower tooth sits outside the upper jaw in a notch (crocodile), snout tapers to a V (vs alligator U).
mistakes: Tail too short or too round in section; it should be about 1.4x the trunk and laterally flattened.
Legs too long and tucked under the body like a dinosaur or lizard; limbs stay low with the belly on the ground at rest.
Head too narrow and tall, teeth hidden; skull is wide and flat with the width ~2.5x the height and teeth visible when the mouth is closed.

must_have: Folded wingtips reach to about the tail tip (bald eagle: level to slightly short; golden eagle: short by ~0.1).
Legs are mostly hidden: feathered tibia 'trousers' cover down to the tarsus; exposed yellow tarsus ~0.2 plus massive toes with the hallux talon ~0.1. Golden eagles are feathered to the toes.
Head: heavy hooked bill ~0.15 with a prominent brow ridge over a forward-set eye; head width ~0.6 of head length; perched body leans ~45 degrees, not vertical.
mistakes: Body too vertical with long exposed bare legs (chicken stance); eagles perch leaning forward on short-looking feathered legs.
Head and bill too small; eagle head is ~0.4 body length and the bill is deep and hooked, not a small songbird beak.
Folded wings too short and tail too long, or primaries drawn as a smooth blob instead of stacked, pointed feather tips crossing near the tail.

must_have: First dorsal origin just behind the pectoral insertion (~0.36), height ~0.12; second dorsal and anal tiny (~0.03) and opposite each other at ~0.75.
Heterocercal tail: upper lobe 0.3, lower lobe 0.5-0.8 of upper (near-symmetric lunate only for white/mako); strong lateral keels on a narrow peduncle (~0.06 deep).
Five gill slits immediately ahead of the pectoral, mouth under the snout at ~0.09 with the eye just above and ahead of it; conical snout, max body depth at ~0.35.
mistakes: First dorsal too far forward over the head or too tall and sickle-like; body too uniformly tubular with a fat tail base.
Tail lobes drawn symmetrical (fish-like) on a requiem/tiger shark, or lower lobe missing entirely.
Mouth drawn at the snout tip or too wide, eyes too large, pectorals too small (they should be ~0.2, as long as the head is tall).

must_have: Hind limb ~1.8x SVL with tibia >= femur; when sitting the folded leg forms a Z with the knee pointing out-and-forward beside the flank and the heel at the vent.
Eyes bulge above the skull profile and are set wide; tympanum visible behind the eye (bullfrog male: larger than the eye); dorsolateral folds / sacral hump break the back silhouette.
Forelimbs short (~0.7 SVL total) with 4 unwebbed fingers; hind feet fully webbed with 5 toes, foot ~0.5 SVL.
mistakes: Hind legs too short and straight (toad-like) with the knee tucked under the body instead of folded out to the side.
Front legs too long and used like arms; the frog's chest sits almost on the ground with the forearms vertical.
Head too narrow and pointed with small eyes; frog head is nearly as wide as the body and the eyes are the dominant feature.

must_have: Elephantine columnar legs directly under the shell: forelimbs flattened and armoured with large scales, bending at the elbow so the foot plants forward; hind legs round pillars. Not paddles.
Scute map: 5 vertebral, 4 costal each side, 11 marginals each side, 1 nuchal; growth rings on each scute; shell front edge flares over the neck, rear marginals flare over the tail.
Head is small (~0.22) with a blunt beaked snout and eye ~0.3 of head length; neck retracts straight back (S-curve vertical), not sideways.
mistakes: Turtle legs (splayed, flippery) and a turtle-flat shell; tortoise shell is high-domed (~0.5 of length) and legs are vertical pillars.
Head too big and lizard-like with a long neck; head stays ~1/5 of shell length.
Shell drawn as a smooth hemisphere with random hexagons; the plastron also too small or shell too narrow (width ~0.8 of length).

must_have: Hind foot ~0.65 lying flat on the ground from heel to the 4th-toe claw; tibia ~0.8 (the longest bone); massive thigh ~0.5 long and ~0.33 wide in side view.
Tail ~= body length, very thick at the base (~0.25 diameter) tapering evenly; it rests on the ground as the third leg of the tripod with the body weight on the heels.
Forelimbs tiny (~0.7 total, 1/2.7 of hind), held bent against the chest with 5 clawed fingers; long narrow muzzle, big upright ears ~0.23, spine curved and leaning forward ~40 degrees.
mistakes: Forearms too large and human-like, or shoulders too broad; the chest is narrow and the arms are small (big arms only on boomer males, and still < hind limb/2).
Tail too thin at the base or lifted off the ground at rest; base girth is almost as thick as the thigh.
Posture too vertical with the hock lifted (dog-like), hind foot too short; at rest the whole foot from heel to toe is planted and the spine curves forward.
